text:
sasha: Quick follow-up from the onboarding RFC — I sketched a small "graceful-degrade" playbook for the intake pipeline. Goal: keep customer traffic alive when a new model fails bench or runtime checks, with clear rollback and probe signals.

neil: drop the sketch pls, want to see how this interacts with canary windows.

sasha: pasted the flow below. TL;DR: 1) intake -> lightweight probe -> canary traffic (10%) -> bench + runtime smoke in parallel -> if bench fails, route 100% back to last-good model, mark model as "quarantine"; if runtime latency regresses, try delayed KV-warmup + reduced batch until stable.

tara: sounds reasonable. question: who owns the "quarantine" state? is it model-registry metadata or the ingress routing layer?

sasha: proposal: quarantine flag in model-registry (authoritative), routing layer subscribes. reasons: single source of truth for UI/rollout, easier to persist reason+metrics.

neil: +1. also add an automated postmortem trigger for any quarantine event (bench failure or >p95 latency+error spike). we should capture a snapshot of the probe inputs and the eval diff.

_dmitri: concern:_ automatic fallback might mask flaky regressions if bench is noisy. we should add a hysteresis: require 2 independent failing probes within 15 min OR a failure + human ack for certain severity.

bench-bot: bench run queued: model=epoch-2023-11-22, probe_set=smoke-quick, expected_time=45s. result: FAILURE (regression in perplexity on golden set: +4.2%).

neil: bench-bot result -> good example. With that, route back full traffic, mark quarantine, and spawn immediate "replay" job against full smoke suite. Also: annotate the quarantine with the bench run id and link to artifacts.

sasha: added a quick rollout config snippet for the router:

```
# router rollout policy (proposal)
routes:
  - model: epoch-2023-11-22
    canary_pct: 10
    probe_policy: quick-smoke
    fallback: last_good_model
    quarantine_on: [bench_failure, runtime_latency_regression]
    quarantine_hysteresis: { failures: 2, window_minutes: 15 }
```

tara: minor nit: we should separate "quarantine_on" causes into fast (auto quarantine) vs slow (needs human). bench_failure -> auto, semantic-regression -> human?

sasha: agreed. will split causes into auto_quarantine and manual_review in the final version.

neil: operational notes: add an SLI that tracks fraction of quarantine-induced rollbacks per week and alert if >1% of rollouts. Also add a dashboard tile showing canary pass/fail over last 24h.

dmitri: final ask: what is the default backoff strategy when latency regresses? we talked about KV warmup and batch reduction, but need deterministic steps.

sasha: proposed deterministic remediation sequence: 1) KV warmup window (5min prefix cache prefill), 2) reduce batch_size by 25% (to a min), 3) fall back to lower-capacity quantized binary if available, 4) fallback to last_good_model. each step runs for 5 min and requires success criteria (p50/p95 within SLO).

neil: can we make that sequence pluggable per-customer? enterprise customers might want different thresholds.

sasha: yes — rollout policy supports overrides per-tenant. default lives in platform config, tenant overrides in dedicated config.

tara: action items?

sasha: I will: 1) update the RFC doc with quarantine_owner=registry + split of auto/manual causes, 2) add router config schema example, 3) write the postmortem webhook spec. ETA EOD tomorrow.

neil: I'll add SLI/alert tickets and the dashboard tile.

dmitri: I'll draft the hysteresis tests for the probe harness (flaky bench simulation).

bench-bot: reminder: scheduled bench sweep for newly onboarded models at 02:00 UTC daily.

sasha: thanks — filing a follow-up PR with the router schema and tests, pinging @eng-oncall if any automated quarantine triggers during rollout tests. ✅
